title: Slain convict was labelled high risk: Attacked police with two knives: [FINAL C Edition]
article: An inmate who was released from federal jail despite staff fears he was a high risk for future violence was shot a dozen times three days later by junior Vancouver police officers after he attacked them with two steak knives.
Gerald Chenery, 29, was turned away from 11 different halfway houses after his release two days before Christmas 2004 because of his violent tendencies, a coroner's inquest heard yesterday.
At the time of his death, police said the officers, both first- year rookies, shot at Chenery 15 times, hitting him 12 times, because he was attacking them with knives.
Police called it a "life and death" situation. The officers were not charged.
Constables Beth Clark and Bryan Smith are scheduled to testify at the inquest today.

The coroner and five jurors heard yesterday that Mission Institution staff had concerns about releasing Chenery on statutory release. He had been sentenced to two and a half years for robbing the Virgin record store in Vancouver five times in 11 days.
"We'd all agreed Gerald Chenery was a high risk to reoffend," said parole officer Sam Beaton.
Chenery, who had substance abuse problems, was required to abstain from drugs and alcohol and to live in a halfway house.

Chenery, who came from Prince Rupert, told Beaton he wanted to return to the north. But the request was denied because of the lack of halfway houses, treatment centres and parole officers there, the inquest heard.

His sister Teresa Chenery, 31, who attended the inquest with siblings Sylvia Fee, 29, and Edith Fee, 28, and other supporters, said her brother was looking forward to getting to know his family again and join their father on a trapline up north.
"Gerald wanted a better life," she said.
